content.question: Why do data points become increasingly sparse in high-dimensional spaces?
options: The number of points required to maintain a given density grows exponentially with the number of dimensions.
The number of points required to maintain a given density grows linearly with the number of dimensions.
High dimensions cause data points to compress closer to each other.
Algorithms automatically discard redundant features in high dimensions.
content.answer: The number of points required to maintain a given density grows exponentially with the number of dimensions.
